title: The leak scan misses a narrow-wrapped EC key body whose first line starts with //
goal: kbcommon.leak_hits flags a narrow-wrapped (8 to 19 characters per line) EC key body whose first three lines include one that starts with //, as it flags the same body without the //

run:
import sys
def _fail(t, e, tb, _d=sys.excepthook):
    if issubclass(t, AssertionError):
        print("check failed:", e)
        sys.exit(1)
    _d(t, e, tb)
sys.excepthook = _fail
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import kbcommon
d = "-" * 5
arm = d + "BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY" + d
hit = lambda t: any(k == "secret" for k, _ in kbcommon.leak_hits(t))
cases = {"slash_first": arm + "\n//8x89Kh\nAb12Cd34\nZy98Wx76", "slash_nine": arm + "\n//8x89Khm\nAb12Cd34\nZy98Wx76"}
miss = [k for k, v in cases.items() if not hit(v)]
print("narrow-wrapped bodies with a // first line that pass:", miss)
sys.exit(1 if miss else 0)

notes: Found by the SP-swavez3g review (S3) of BG-ok4itunr: the gap between the armor line and the body eats the // as a comment prefix and the line drops under 8 characters; 3 of 4000 random 8-character bodies were missed.
